name: Lucy McBath
page_title: Lucy McBath's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (GA) - District 6

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "50 years ago, the Roe v. Wade decision provided a constitutional right to abortion. That right is now under attack.In @HouseJudiciary, I shared the heartbreak that comes with a miscarriage. Without Roe, all reproductive care is on the line.We can't back down in this fight."
"A year ago, the Dobbs decision overturned Roe v. Wade and allowed states to begin attacking the reproductive care that so many women rely on."

"Fortunately, the courts are upholding women's rights around the country. A federal court overturned Georgia's extreme abortion ban earlier this month. We will never stop the fight to protect Roe v. Wade in Washington."

"Good news -- Governor Kemp's extreme abortion ban in GA won't go into effect on 1/1/20, but we have to keep defending Roe v. Wade here and in Washington D.C. We'll keep fighting until every woman can make her own reproductive healthcare decisions."

positions.question: Do you support a decrease in income taxes in order to balance the budget?

evidence.text: "Instead, I favor focusing on the middle class and working families. In addition to making middle class tax cuts permanent, I want to increase the minimum wage and making the federal earned income tax credit more generous. Growing up, I was taught that if you are able and willing to put in hard work in America, you should be able to earn a living wage. No one in Cobb, DeKalb, or Fulton Counties can comfortably live on $7.25 an hour."

"This historic investment will set us on a course to create millions of good-paying jobs, lower health care costs for our communities, provide tax cuts to hard-working families, and get Americans back to work and America back to normal."
Rated 8% by National Taxpayers Union
Voted in favor of HR 5377 "Restoring Tax Fairness for States and Localities Act"

positions.question: Do you support the regulation of indirect campaign contributions from corporations, unions, and individuals?

evidence.text: "Congresswoman McBath strongly believes in the need for campaign finance reform and strengthening voting rights. As a member of the House Judiciary Committee, the Congresswoman advocates for reforming voting rights, civil liberties, and the criminal justice system. One of her first actions in Congress was to co-sponsor H.R. 1, the For the People Act, a bill that would enact landmark campaign finance reforms to our democratic process."
Rated 100% by End Citizens United
Rated 94% by Common Cause
Voted in favor of HR 1 "For the People Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support protecting government officials, including law enforcement officers, from personal liability in civil lawsuits concerning alleged misconduct?

evidence.text: "A year ago today George Floyd was murdered. Nothing will bring him back or erase the pain Americans have felt for generations as a direct result of a broken system. We have put forward legislation to reform our laws, and now we must pass it. Lives depend on it."

"I am so proud of our many officers in Georgia's Sixth District, here in the Capitol Building, and those nationwide who do all they can to keep our families safe. They have the trust of their communities, and as a result are better at ensuring everyone's safety," said McBath. "This bill is about making sure every officer and every department is held to the high standard set by officers like these. By passing the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, we ensure all of our police officers have the resources to become our very best police officers, and that will make every one of us safer."

"We must continue to hold our government accountable for their actions. We must continue to hold this administration accountable for their actions. We must continue to fight for transparency, accountability, and oversight."
Voted in favor of HR 1280 "George Floyd Justice in Policing Act of 2021"

positions.question: Do you support increasing defense spending?

evidence.text: "Our service men and women sacrifice so much to protect our country, our citizens, and our freedoms," said McBath. "My father, brother, and nephew all served this nation in uniform, and I am committed to the unwavering support of those who defend this nation and our values."
Voted in favor of HR 2670 "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024"
Voted in favor of S 1605 "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022."

"Glad my bipartisan amendment was included in the #NDAA! The bill passed & provides:a pay raise to our troops "safe-to-report" policy to allow sexual assault victims report w/out fear strong congressional oversight a robust defense budget"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

evidence.text: "Congresswoman McBath has made lowering student debt a priority because it too often holds students and graduates back. She supports fully funding K-12 education and making public universities, vocational schools, and community colleges more affordable."
"ICYMI: This week, I introduced the #ReliefAct2019 to #DefendStudents & provide opportunities for student debt relief after misconduct by institutions."

"In #GA06, Argosy closed & ripped off hundreds of kids, leaving them with huge student debt. Our children should be leaving school ready for success, not paying for the misconduct of institutions. Today, we voted to protect students & reverse the DeVos rule. #StandWithStudents"
"She also supports measures expanding access to higher education, fully funding public schools, and making community colleges and vocational schools more affordable for all of our children."

positions.question: Do you support requiring a government-issued identification in order to vote at the polls?

evidence.text: "Ten years ago, the Shelby County ruling opened the floodgates to voting discrimination with an intensity that has only continued. Voting rights protect all other rights, and today we fight on to protect and exercise the fundamental right to vote. #ShelbyAt10"
"The Voting Rights Act turns 55 today. We must each commit to the VRA's legacy to ensure that all Americans have access to the ballot box."
Voted in favor of HR 4 "John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act of 2021"
Voted in favor of HR 5746 "Freedom to vote: John R. Lewis Act"

positions.question: Do you support a government-run (e.g. single-payer) healthcare program, such as Medicare-for-All?

evidence.text: "As a two-time breast cancer survivor who lives with pre-existing conditions, and a daughter of two medical professionals, Congresswoman McBath understands the importance of quality, affordable health care. No family should have to worry about choosing between paying their bills and paying for healthcare. She supports proposals making it easier for more Georgians to get covered and to expand upon the Affordable Care Act (ACA). Moreover, her tireless efforts in Congress sent the Centers for Disease Control additional pandemic related funding to protect the health of our entire communities."

"I have beaten breast cancer twice - I know how important it is that we fight to cover those with pre-existing conditions. That is why today I proudly voted to defend the #ACA, and to make it easier to get quality and affordable health insurance."
Voted in favor of HR 1425 "Patient Protection and Affordable Care Enhancement Act"
